paras.en: While bacteria in soil produce geosmin, plants discharge aromatic oils during a drought to create a shield to protect against harsh heat and minimize water loss. When raindrops hit dry ground and plants, the impact creates microscopic bubbles filled with geosmin and oils that rise into the air, pop and scatter into tiny particles that can then fill human nostrils.
paras.zh: 土壤中的细菌会产生土臭素，而植物在干旱期间会释放芳香油，以形成屏障，抵御酷热并最大限度地减少水分流失。当雨滴撞击干燥的地面和植物时，撞击会产生充满土臭素和油的微小气泡，这些气泡上升到空气中，破裂并分散成微小颗粒，然后填充人类鼻孔。

paras.en: Exactly how petrichor changes will depend on where you are as the effects of rising global temperatures on weather and climate patterns will vary from place to place and year to year. Overall, parts of the world that get more rainfall will experience less petrichor, whereas areas that have droughts will experience more, says Jeppe Lund Nielsen, a professor of microbial physiology at Aalborg University in Denmark.
paras.zh: Petrichor 的具体变化方式取决于您所在的位置，因为全球气温上升对天气和气候模式的影响因地而异、因年而异。丹麦奥尔堡大学微生物生理学教授 Jeppe Lund Nielsen 表示，总体而言，世界上降雨量较多的地区会出现较少的石斑病，而干旱的地区则会出现较多的石斑病。

paras.en: Droughts cause geosmin to build up, and when they occur with hotter temperatures, bacteria produce even more geosmin as heat speeds up chemical reactions inside the microbes. “If you get a higher temperature, you also get a higher production of the compounds,” Nielsen says. So when it finally does rain, more geosmin is released. But if soils get too dry, “the geosmin will dry up and not be released,” Lundström says.
paras.zh: 干旱会导致土臭素积聚，当温度升高时，由于热量会加速微生物内部的化学反应，细菌会产生更多的土臭素。 “如果温度更高，化合物的产量也会更高，”尼尔森说。因此，当最终下雨时，会释放出更多的土臭素。但如果土壤变得太干燥，“土臭素就会干涸而不会被释放，”伦德斯特罗姆说。

paras.en: Where rain falls more frequently, there will be less petrichor because the aromatic compounds won’t have enough time to accumulate. And heavy downpours—which are increasing as the planet warms—are too forceful to trap the tiny air bubbles required to launch the scent into the air. Instead the compounds are diluted, pushed underground or mixed in surface floodwaters.
paras.zh: 在降雨频繁的地方，石质物质会较少，因为芳香化合物没有足够的时间积聚。随着地球变暖，倾盆大雨变得越来越猛烈，无法捕获将气味散发到空气中所需的微小气泡。相反，这些化合物被稀释、推入地下或混合在地表洪水中。

paras.en: Soil degradation—which has also increased as a result of higher temperatures and heavier downpours—plays a role, too, because it means fewer geosmin-producing bacteria can grow.
paras.zh: 土壤退化（由于气温升高和倾盆大雨而加剧）也起到了一定作用，因为这意味着能够生长的产生土臭素的细菌会减少。

paras.en: Any changes to geosmin won’t stop at what humans smell. Insects that react to petrichor will also have to adjust their behavior, Nielsen says. For example, areas with large amounts of petrichor will likely see an increase in mosquitoes, because the smell indicates to these insects that the dry ground is now a moist fertile environment in which to lay their eggs.
paras.zh: 土臭素的任何变化都不会止于人类的气味。尼尔森说，对石斑病有反应的昆虫也必须调整它们的行为。例如，在有大量臭虫的地区，蚊子的数量可能会增加，因为气味向这些昆虫表明，干燥的地面现在是一个潮湿肥沃的环境，可以产卵。

articles.title: Democratic Michigan Senate hopeful Abdul El-Sayed explains how science influences his politics

paras.en: The 2026 U.S. midterm elections are just weeks away. Among the highest-profile races is the contest for Michigan’s open Senate seat. With Senator Gary Peters not seeking reelection, the Democratic candidate is Abdul El-Sayed, who holds degrees in both medicine and public health and previously served as the head of Detroit’s public health department.
paras.zh: 距离 2026 年美国中期选举只有几周时间了。最引人注目的竞选之一是密歇根州参议院空缺席位的争夺。由于参议员加里·彼得斯（Gary Peters）不寻求连任，民主党候选人是阿卜杜勒·埃尔·赛义德（Abdul El-Sayed），他拥有医学和公共卫生学位，曾担任底特律公共卫生部门负责人。

paras.en: We asked El-Sayed how his scientific background affects his policy decisions, what the “Make America Healthy Again” (MAHA) movement has gotten right and wrong and what his vision for Medicare for All is.
paras.zh: 我们询问了埃尔-赛义德，他的科学背景如何影响他的政策决策、“让美国再次健康”(MAHA) 运动的对错以及他对全民医疗保险的愿景是什么。

paras.en: [An edited transcript of the interview follows.]
paras.zh: [编辑后的采访记录如下。]

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: How has your background in science influenced your thinking on policy in general?
paras.zh: 您的科学背景如何影响您对总体政策的思考？

paras.en: I’m a systems scientist. That’s how I trained. I wrote my doctoral thesis on systems in epidemiologic research. Every good scientific inquiry starts with a great question, and I think so much of what’s wrong with public policy starts with a great question: Why don’t we have health care when we need it? Why is there such massive inequity? What is the best way to allocate our scarce resources? How do we take on the challenges of a world in which there’s too much violence and too little peace?
paras.zh: 我是一名系统科学家。我就是这样训练的。我写了关于流行病学研究系统的博士论文。每一个好的科学研究都始于一个伟大的问题，我认为公共政策的许多问题都始于一个伟大的问题：为什么我们在需要时没有医疗保健？为什么存在如此巨大的不平等？分配稀缺资源的最佳方式是什么？我们如何应对这个暴力太多、和平太少的世界的挑战？

paras.en: The thing about science is that you construct a hypothesis of the world and you test it. I think that that level of rigor—to ask, “What is the nature of this problem? How do I integrate data about the problem? How do I answer this? And then how do I work this in terms of the political process and the policymaking process?”—all of that creates living labs where we try to build the world that we all want to live in, a place that’s more peaceful, where more people have the things that they need and deserve, where we can live together in harmony. Once you train in the sciences, you don’t leave that scientific approach to thinking and that rigor of thinking. And I try to bring that to policy problems.
paras.zh: 关于科学的事情是你构建一个世界假设并测试它。我认为这种严格程度——问“这个问题的本质是什么？我如何整合有关该问题的数据？我如何回答这个问题？然后我如何在政治进程和决策过程中解决这个问题？”——所有这些都创造了一个活生生的实验室，我们试图建设一个我们都想生活的世界，一个更加和平的地方，让更多的人拥有他们需要和应得的东西，我们可以和谐地生活在一起。一旦你接受了科学训练，你就不会放弃科学的思维方法和严谨的思维。我试图将其带入政策问题。

paras.en: A lot of what science does is descriptive rather than prescriptive, so it can be a little bit of a jump from one to the other. So can you elaborate on how you take that kind of “rigor of thinking,” as you said, and then apply it to solutions that the data suggest will work?
paras.zh: 科学所做的很多事情都是描述性的，而不是规定性的，所以它可能会有点从一个到另一个的跳跃。那么，您能否详细说明一下如何采用您所说的那种“严谨的思维”，然后将其应用到数据表明有效的解决方案中？

paras.en: Well, you know, it’s true [science] is descriptive. But every question that we ask in science is to design an intervention, right? We don’t just ask these questions because they’re fun to ask.... They are fun to ask and answer, but we ask them because we do want to make things better. Why do we want to understand the way that the body breaks down glucose? Why do we want to understand what the appendix measure doesn’t do? Because we want to do something about it, right? We want to design anything that addresses the problem. We want to understand what the implications of removing an appendix might be.
paras.zh: 嗯，你知道，[科学]确实是描述性的。但我们在科学中提出的每一个问题都是为了设计干预措施，对吗？我们问这些问题不仅仅是因为问起来很有趣……问和回答这些问题很有趣，但我们问这些问题是因为我们确实想让事情变得更好。为什么我们要了解身体分解葡萄糖的方式？为什么我们想要了解附录措施不能做什么？因为我们想为此做点什么，对吗？我们想要设计任何能够解决问题的东西。我们想了解切除阑尾可能会产生什么影响。

paras.en: I think it’s important to remember that, in science, it’s not that we’re just descriptive; it’s that we are descriptive so that we might be prescriptive in an evidence-driven and thoughtful fashion. I think it’s the same approach in public policy, where you want to understand the system, but you want to understand the system so as to intervene, and then it’s iterative; it’s recursive. You will engage your current understanding of the problem, you’ll pose an intervention, and then you’ll study the outcome of the intervention to see if it works.
paras.zh: 我认为重要的是要记住，在科学中，我们不仅仅是描述性的；我们只是描述性的。我们是描述性的，因此我们可以以证据驱动和深思熟虑的方式做出规定。我认为这在公共政策中也是同样的方法，你想要了解这个系统，但你想要了解这个系统以便进行干预，然后它是迭代的；它是递归的。您将结合您当前对问题的理解，提出干预措施，然后研究干预的结果，看看它是否有效。

paras.en: As we’re building and designing interventions, it is about being willing to say, “Okay, this worked really well. Here’s the next thing we can do to make it even better.” And it’s that ability to continue after the problem until we’ve gotten solutions that really are purpose fit. Understanding that the world also evolves and changes, that the nature of the problem today might change as a function of what you did but also of other forces that are shaping the problem.
paras.zh: 当我们构建和设计干预措施时，我们要愿意说：“好吧，这真的很有效。这是我们下一步可以做的事情，让它变得更好。”正是这种在问题出现后继续下去的能力，直到我们得到真正适合目的的解决方案。了解世界也在不断发展和变化，当今问题的性质可能会因您所做的事情以及造成问题的其他力量而发生变化。

paras.en: Your expertise is largely in public health. You’ve spoken a lot about the structural and social determinants of health, but it can take a long time for systemic change to occur. The effects may only be felt years down the line. How does pushing for those changes help people right now?
paras.zh: 您的专业知识主要集中在公共卫生领域。您已经谈了很多关于健康的结构性和社会决定因素，但系统性变革可能需要很长时间才能发生。其影响可能要在几年后才能感受到。推动这些变革对人们现在有何帮助？

paras.en: That’s the thing: you have to make sure it does help people in the place and the time in which the pain is being felt the hardest. I think that’s the thing about it..., that, too often, people can’t wait for the system to change. You have to think in the system, but you also have to be thinking about the issue. And I think the best analogy here is in medicine.
paras.zh: 事情就是这样：你必须确保它确实能帮助那些在痛苦最严重的地方和时间的人们。我认为这就是问题所在……人们常常迫不及待地等待系统改​​变。你必须在制度中思考，但你也必须思考问题。我认为这里最好的类比是医学。

paras.en: It’s one thing to say we’re going to cure your cancer, but we also have to heal your pain right now because that pain is the most acute symptom of what the long term might be doing to you. It’s thinking in time and place, both about addressing the system and also addressing the most acute manifestations of a broken system, and you’ve got to do both at the same time.
paras.zh: 说我们要治愈您的癌症是一回事，但我们现在也必须治愈您的疼痛，因为疼痛是长期可能对您造成的最严重的症状。它是在时间和地点进行思考，既要解决系统问题，也要解决损坏系统的最严重的表现，而且你必须同时做这两件事。

paras.en: Can you elaborate on what systems, outside of direct health care, need to change to let Americans have healthier lives?
paras.zh: 您能否详细说明一下，除了直接医疗保健之外，还需要改变哪些系统才能让美国人过上更健康的生活？

paras.en: Think about our energy systems. We could be providing high-quality, renewable energy that does not force us to breathe from the ends of a smokestack, that is both more affordable and more accessible. But we don’t do that because of the power of a few corporations to dominate that system and to continue to sell us stuff that is less efficient and less effective.
paras.zh: 想想我们的能源系统。我们可以提供高质量的可再生能源，这种能源不会迫使我们从烟囱末端呼吸，而且更便宜，也更容易获得。但我们之所以不这样做，是因为少数公司有能力主导这个系统，并继续向我们出售效率较低、效果较差的东西。

paras.en: Think about the system of inequality in this country. How do you make sure that a few corporations can’t just rig the system to continue to put it in overdrive so that they make more and extract more from us? You think about the impact of tech, in the way that we build tech policy. Amazing science goes into building really great tech. But at the same time, what is driving that? What are the incentives driving that? Are we building artificial intelligence (AI) to take away our jobs and win a race that might end up destroying us all, or are we building AI as a tool that empowers us in our lives? And how do you get the incentives of that right?
paras.zh: 想想这个国家的不平等制度。你如何确保少数公司不能只是操纵系统继续超速运转，以便他们从我们身上赚更多钱并榨取更多钱？你会以我们制定技术政策的方式来思考技术的影响。令人惊奇的科学有助于构建真正伟大的技术。但与此同时，是什么推动了这一趋势？推动这一趋势的动机是什么？我们构建人工智能（AI）是为了抢走我们的工作并赢得一场可能最终毁灭我们所有人的竞赛，还是将人工智能构建为一种赋予我们生活力量的工具？如何获得正确的激励措施？

paras.en: Across the board, there is a structural process that you have to think through but also key consequences that you have to adjust around, even in the short term.
paras.zh: 总的来说，有一个你必须仔细考虑的结构性过程，但也有你必须调整的关键后果，即使是在短期内。

paras.en: There’s some overlap there between health policies you’re proposing and those put forward by the MAHA movement. What do you make of MAHA?
paras.zh: 您提出的卫生政策与 MAHA 运动提出的卫生政策之间存在一些重叠。你觉得玛哈怎么样？

paras.en: I think it is a consequence of a few people exploiting the distrust of a system that has earned that distrust. The reason that people distrust science isn’t because they don’t trust science. We use science every day. It’s because they don’t trust the corporations that hold that science. You’re paying more and more for insulin that’s existed for 100 years. It’s not a far leap to go from “I don’t trust these corporations because I can’t afford the things that they are making” to “I don’t even trust the things that they’re making,” and I think MAHA has been a response to that.
paras.zh: 我认为这是少数人利用对一个已经赢得不信任的体系的不信任的结果。人们不信任科学的原因并不是因为他们不信任科学。我们每天都在运用科学。这是因为他们不信任拥有这项科学的公司。您为已经存在 100 年的胰岛素支付的费用越来越高。从“我不信任这些公司，因为我买不起他们正在制造的东西”到“我什至不信任他们正在制造的东西”，这并不是一个很大的飞跃，我认为 MAHA 就是对此的回应。

paras.en: I think what people really want is: they want to be healthy. And I think science has always been the best arbiter about how to make people healthy. The problem is: we’ve got to make sure that the scientific discoveries that we put forward are also affordable to people so they can actually have them.
paras.zh: 我认为人们真正想要的是：他们想要健康。我认为科学始终是如何使人们健康的最佳仲裁者。问题是：我们必须确保我们提出的科学发现也是人们负担得起的，这样他们才能真正拥有它们。

paras.en: How do you draw the line between skepticism, which is part of the scientific process, and rejecting evidence, which is something we’ve seen MAHA spokespeople and figures do?
paras.zh: 您如何区分怀疑主义（科学过程的一部分）和拒绝证据（我们看到 MAHA 发言人和人物所做的事情）？

paras.en: It’s faulty and dangerous to reject evidence, and you’ve got to push back on that. How do we build the kind of health policy that takes on the evidence-based ways that corporations are making us sicker, whether it’s pollutants in our environment or additives that should not be added to our foods, or to the ultraprocessed food environment?
paras.zh: 拒绝证据是错误且危险的，你必须反驳这一点。我们如何制定一种健康政策，以基于证据的方式看待企业让我们病情加重的情况，无论是环境中的污染物还是不应添加到我们的食品或超加工食品环境中的添加剂？

paras.en: Meanwhile vaccines have done some really, really great things, and there’s no evidence to suggest that, on net, they’re causing more harm than good. And so I think you’ve just got to hear the scientific process. The problem, though, is that, too often, we don’t act on a lot of the problems that we do have evidence for, and it creates a level of skepticism. I’m trying to just lead us where the evidence goes.
paras.zh: 与此同时，疫苗确实做了一些非常非常伟大的事情，而且没有证据表明它们在网络上造成的弊大于利。所以我认为你只需要听听科学过程即可。但问题是，我们常常没有对很多我们确实有证据支持的问题采取行动，这会产生一定程度的怀疑。我试图引导我们找到证据。

paras.en: One thing your health policy agenda doesn’t touch on is glyphosate, which is a major issue for many MAHA followers. Where do you stand on that?
paras.zh: 您的卫生政策议程没有触及的一件事是草甘膦，这对许多 MAHA 追随者来说是一个主要问题。你对此持什么立场？

paras.en: I’ll be honest: I didn’t take a very direct position on that because I need to understand the science a little bit better. I want to be led by science, and I also understand the deep concerns that folks have.
paras.zh: 老实说：我对此并没有采取非常直接的立场，因为我需要更好地理解科学。我希望以科学为指导，我也理解人们的深切关注。

paras.en: I think we need to err on the side of caution. But we also need to make sure that science drives our positions. And we need to be able to demonstrate the potential impacts over time.
paras.zh: 我认为我们需要谨慎行事。但我们还需要确保科学推动我们的立场。我们需要能够随着时间的推移展示潜在的影响。

paras.en: But part of the problem is just the way that we set scientific data standards. In the U.S., too many of our standards are “innocent until proven guilty,” and I think that when it comes to broad health concerns, you really need to demonstrate that something is safe before you start putting it in all of our foodstuffs. I think that is part of the challenge that the broader MAHA movement has been concerned about. I know there’s a lot of controversy around these particular sets of chemicals, but I want to be able to really review the science, understand where we sit and then apply that principle. We need to be able to demonstrate that this is definitely safe rather than assuming it’s safe until we’re proven wrong, like all these PFAS chemicals [perfluoroalkyl and polyfluoroalkyl substances, or “forever chemicals”] that only later science has demonstrated are so dangerous.
paras.zh: 但部分问题在于我们制定科学数据标准的方式。在美国，我们的太多标准都是“在被证明有罪之前是无辜的”，我认为，当涉及到广泛的健康问题时，在开始将某种东西添加到我们所有的食品中之前，你确实需要证明它是安全的。我认为这是更广泛的 MAHA 运动所关注的挑战的一部分。我知道围绕这些特定的化学物质存在很多争议，但我希望能够真正回顾科学，了解我们所处的位置，然后应用该原则。我们需要能够证明这绝对是安全的，而不是假设它是安全的，直到我们被证明是错误的，就像所有这些 PFAS 化学品 [全氟烷基和多氟烷基物质，或“永远的化学品”]，直到后来的科学才证明它们是如此危险。

paras.en: A lot of your positions require well-staffed enforcement agencies, which have gone through large-scale cuts. What can be done to beef them up, given that it’s clear that’s not where the administration’s priorities lie?
paras.zh: 许多职位都需要人员配备齐全的执法机构，而这些机构已经经历了大规模裁员。鉴于这显然不是政府的优先事项，可以采取哪些措施来加强它们？

paras.en: We’re going to need to reinvest in these agencies—and not just reinvest but modernize and make sure that we’re not just building back. We need to build forward the agencies that we need for the 21st century. They’ve taken a gigantic scalpel—no, forget a scalpel—[they’ve] taken a chainsaw to these agencies, and we’re going to need to be invested appropriately so that we can we can start to enforce where we need to. Whether it’s the [Food and Drug Administration or the Environmental Protection Agency], reinvesting in [the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention or the National Institutes of Health], we are going to have to do that.
paras.zh: 我们需要对这些机构进行再投资——不仅仅是再投资，而是实现现代化，并确保我们不仅仅是重建。我们需要建设 21 世纪所需的机构。他们拿了一把巨大的手术刀——不，忘了手术刀——[他们]对这些机构拿了一把电锯，我们需要进行适当的投资，这样我们就可以开始在需要的地方强制执行。无论是[食品和药物管理局还是环境保护局]，还是对[疾病控制和预防中心或美国国立卫生研究院]进行再投资，我们都必须这样做。

paras.en: We’re going to need people who both understand and have been to these agencies before they ever got elected and also can be sitting with experts to say, “If we could build what we need, not just what we’ve had, what would that look like?”
paras.zh: 我们需要那些在当选之前就了解并去过这些机构的人，并且能够与专家坐在一起说：“如果我们能够构建我们需要的东西，而不仅仅是我们已经拥有的东西，那会是什么样子？”

paras.en: What can be accomplished may hinge on the outcome of the presidential election in 2028. If you’re elected in the midterms, is there anything that you plan to do from your position in the Senate over the next two years?
paras.zh: 能完成什么，可能取决于2028年总统选举的结果。如果你在中期选举中当选，未来两年你在参议院的职位上有什么计划吗？

paras.en: I think it’s worth reviewing a lot of the way that [the U.S. DOGE Service] happened and asking how much of that was actually legal and understanding what that is.
paras.zh: 我认为值得回顾一下 [美国 DOGE 服务] 的发生方式，并询问其中有多少实际上是合法的，并了解那是什么。

paras.en: I wish I could tell you [that], from the U.S. Senate, I could I could snap my fingers and take it back to where it was. That’s just not where we are. We have to leverage the political process to build what we need. From the U.S. Senate, there’s a lot of lawmaking we can do that I hope would pass both houses. Now, if Donald Trump wants to veto, he can. But all that’ll do is demonstrate the pressure that needs to be put on him and demonstrate exactly how frankly mendacious he has been when it comes to the proper function of government.
paras.zh: 我希望我能从美国参议院告诉你，我可以打个响指，把它带回原来的地方。那不是我们现在的处境。我们必须利用政治进程来建设我们所需要的东西。在美国参议院，我们可以制定很多立法，我希望这些立法能够获得参众两院的通过。现在，如果唐纳德·特朗普想要否决，他可以。但所做的一切只是表明需要向他施加的压力，并准确地表明他在政府正常运作方面是多么坦率地撒谎。

paras.en: We’ve heard from people who are not in the scientific community who believe that getting government out of research isn’t necessarily a bad thing, that we should get private industry funding basic research. If you’re elected to the Senate, what will your position be?
paras.zh: 我们从科学界以外的人那里听说，让政府退出研究并不一定是坏事，我们应该让私营企业资助基础研究。如果您当选参议院议员，您的职位是什么？

paras.en: We need to restore funding, but it also needs to be built to what it should be. It’s not enough to go back. You talk to anybody in science, they’ll tell you that NIH money is really important, but too often the way that the NIH works is an anachronism to how science actually works right now. Another point I’ll make is that these cuts may seem harmless until you’ve got 8,000 people who are infected with Cyclospora, and people are trying to dodge lettuce in the United States of America. I think it’s important for us to put a name on the consequences and start to address them.
paras.zh: 我们需要恢复资金，但也需要将其建设到应有的水平。回去还不够。你和任何从事科学工作的人交谈，他们会告诉你 NIH 的资金确实很重要，但 NIH 的运作方式往往与当前科学的实际运作方式不合时宜。我要指出的另一点是，这些削减可能看起来无害，直到有 8,000 人感染环孢子虫，并且美国的人们试图避开生菜。我认为对我们来说重要的是要明确后果并开始解决它们。

paras.en: You are a vocal proponent for Medicare for All. Depending on where one gets their numbers, between 800,000 to up to three million people are employed either in health insurance or in fields adjacent to health insurance. How would you approach implementing Medicare for All while limiting mass layoffs in these industries, especially as AI puts pressure on workers?
paras.zh: 您是全民医疗保险的大力支持者。根据统计数据的来源，有 80 万到 300 万人受雇于健康保险或与健康保险相关的领域。您将如何实施全民医疗保险，同时限制这些行业的大规模裁员，特别是在人工智能给工人带来压力的情况下？

paras.en: You’re already seeing a lot of these corporations start using AI to try to eliminate these jobs. While [those job numbers] may be true today, within the next two years, they are coming for those jobs. You’re still going to need people who can process all of the churn that happens, although it’s going to be substantially less. You’re still going to need people in the industry who are doing those jobs.
paras.zh: 你已经看到很多这样的公司开始使用人工智能来试图消除这些工作。虽然[这些工作数字]在今天可能是正确的，但在未来两年内，他们将会来找这些工作。您仍然需要能够处理所有发生的客户流失的人员，尽管这种情况会大大减少。你仍然需要业内人士来做这些工作。

paras.en: The other thing I’ll just tell you is that Medicare for All is going to be a net positive for health care jobs. People right now are working for an industry that makes its money denying people health care. Think about the number of people who exited the current health care system that are going to be repatriated back in when we finally guarantee every single person health care.
paras.zh: 我要告诉你的另一件事是，全民医疗保险将对医疗保健工作产生积极的影响。现在人们正在为一个靠剥夺人们医疗保健而赚钱的行业工作。想想当我们最终保证每个人的医疗保健时，有多少退出当前医疗保健系统的人将被遣返回国。

paras.en: Would that mean importing jobs that are currently in the private sector into the public sector?
paras.zh: 这是否意味着将目前私营部门的就业机会转移到公共部门？

paras.en: No, not necessarily. You’re creating a lot of health care jobs, which will be private. [The idea is to have] public insurance but private health care. Ten percent of the population right now can’t regularly get the health care that they need. Medicare for All would enable them to get that health care, and so you’re going to see massive growth in the private sector to provide health care as paid for by public health insurance.
paras.zh: 不，不一定。你正在创造大量的医疗保健工作，这些工作都是私人的。 [想法是]拥有公共保险但拥有私人医疗保健。目前有百分之十的人口无法定期获得所需的医疗保健。全民医疗保险将使他们能够获得医疗保健，因此您将看到私营部门大幅增长，以提供由公共健康保险支付的医疗保健。

paras.en: Similarly, to your point around the health insurance jobs, you’re going to be able to leverage health insurance. Even Medicare, as it operates right now, there is some subcontracting to private companies that manage some of the paperwork even if the health insurance is still publicly guaranteed. That said, you are going to be able to create a lot of public sector jobs doing a lot of this work. And so the transition will create many more jobs than are lost, mainly via health care, which is going to stay private under Medicare for All.
paras.zh: 同样，就您关于健康保险工作的观点而言，您将能够利用健康保险。即使是目前运作的医疗保险，即使健康保险仍然受到公共保障，也会将一些分包给私人公司来管理一些文书工作。也就是说，您将能够通过做大量此类工作来创造大量公共部门就业机会。因此，这一转变将创造的就业机会远多于失去的就业机会，主要是通过医疗保健，而医疗保健将在全民医疗保险下保持私有。

articles.title: Google’s Project Suncatcher AI data center test has officially launched to space onboard SpaceX rocket

paras.en: Google’s first step toward putting data centers in space is officially underway. On October 1, at approximately 2:32 P.M. EDT, a SpaceX rocket launched an experimental satellite carrying artificial intelligence chips into low-Earth orbit.
paras.zh: 谷歌将数据中心送入太空的第一步已正式启动。 10 月 1 日下午 2:32 左右美国东部时间，SpaceX 的一枚火箭将一颗携带人工智能芯片的实验卫星送入近地轨道。

paras.en: The satellite, Project Suncatcher, is loaded with Google’s Tensor Processing Units (TPUs), chips that the company uses to train and run its AI models. The mission’s goal is to evaluate how the chips fare during the launch, as well as in the hostile space environment.
paras.zh: 这颗名为“Project Suncatcher”的卫星装载了谷歌的张量处理单元（TPU），该公司用这些芯片来训练和运行其人工智能模型。该任务的目标是评估芯片在发射过程中以及在恶劣的太空环境中的表现。

paras.en: The trial TPUs have already been put through their paces on land, with some of the chips subjected to simulated solar radiation and cosmic rays at a proton beam facility at University of California, Davis. In a blog post, Google said that the chips held up “remarkably well” and that the data indicate they could handle more ionizing radiation than what they could be expected to encounter over five years in space.
paras.zh: 试验性 TPU 已经在陆地上进行了测试，其中一些芯片在加州大学戴维斯分校的质子束设施中接受了模拟太阳辐射和宇宙射线的测试。谷歌在一篇博客文章中表示，这些芯片的性能“非常好”，并且数据表明它们可以处理比它们在太空五年内预计会遇到的更多的电离辐射。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: Along with the chips, Project Suncatcher will also test a new cooling system. Because there is no airflow in space, Google’s engineers developed a novel method of dispersing the intense heat generated by TPUs as they perform AI-related functions.
paras.zh: 除了芯片之外，Project Suncatcher 还将测试新的冷却系统。由于太空中没有气流，谷歌的工程师开发了一种新方法来驱散 TPU 在执行人工智能相关功能时产生的高温。

paras.en: Orbital data centers are many AI companies’ answer to the increasingly resource-heavy terrestrial infrastructure required to power AI models—not to mention the fact that ground-based data centers are increasingly politically unpopular. At the same time, these satellite data centers could feasibly harness the nearly unlimited, clean solar energy that an orbital location affords. Aside from Google, OpenAI and xAI are also pushing this idea as a means to solve their Earth-bound problems.
paras.zh: 轨道数据中心是许多人工智能公司针对驱动人工智能模型所需资源日益增多的地面基础设施的解决方案，更不用说地面数据中心在政治上越来越不受欢迎的事实。与此同时，这些卫星数据中心可以切实利用轨道位置提供的几乎无限的清洁太阳能。除了 Google 之外，OpenAI 和 xAI 也在推动这一想法，将其作为解决地球问题的一种手段。

paras.en: Even so, experts caution that there are numerous engineering and cost efficiency challenges that need to be addressed before these plans could be realized. Astronomers have also criticized the plans, saying orbital data centers could contribute to the growing problem of light pollution that’s making observing the night sky increasingly difficult.
paras.zh: 即便如此，专家警告说，在实现这些计划之前，还需要解决许多工程和成本效率挑战。天文学家也批评了这些计划，称轨道数据中心可能会加剧日益严重的光污染问题，使观测夜空变得越来越困难。

paras.en: Google plans to launch two experimental satellites in 2027 to help test how its potential data centers might communicate with one another via lasers.
paras.zh: 谷歌计划在 2027 年发射两颗实验卫星，以帮助测试其潜在数据中心如何通过激光相互通信。

articles.title: Meet the newest living cat species, the first described in 100 years
articles.author: Meghan Rosen

paras.en: Attention cat lovers: There’s an adorable new addition to the feline family tree.
paras.zh: 爱猫人士请注意：猫科动物家族树上又添了一位可爱的新成员。

paras.en: Meet Leopardus tilcayo, a pint-size tiger cat discovered in Bolivia in the Yungas forests of the central Andes Mountains. L. tilcayo, reported September 17 in Current Biology, is the first new living cat species described and named by scientists in more than 100 years. The last one was the Uruguayan pampas cat (L. fasciatus), described in 1923.
paras.zh: 来认识一下 Leopardus tilcayo，这是一种在玻利维亚安第斯山脉中部永加斯森林中发现的小型虎猫。 《当代生物学》9 月 17 日报道的 L. tilcayo 是 100 多年来科学家描述和命名的第一个新的现存猫科动物物种。最后一种是 1923 年描述的乌拉圭潘帕斯猫 (L. fasciatus)。

paras.en: L. tilcayo has a slender body, spotted fur and a ringed tail. It weighs roughly two kilograms, about as much as a two-month-old domestic kitten. For such a tiny cat, L. tilcayo has made a terrific splash, pouncing into headlines around the world. “I did not at all expect attention at this scale,” says Jonas Lescroart, an evolutionary biologist at the University of Antwerp in Belgium.
paras.zh: L. tilcayo 身体细长，皮毛有斑点，尾巴有环。它重约两公斤，相当于一只两个月大的家猫。对于这么小的猫来说，L. tilcayo 却引起了巨大的轰动，登上了世界各地的头条新闻。 “我根本没想到会受到如此大规模的关注，”比利时安特卫普大学的进化生物学家乔纳斯·莱斯科罗特 (Jonas Lescroart) 说。

paras.en: Lescroart and his colleagues hadn’t set out to discover a new species. They were looking to untangle one branch of the cat family tree. Until now, scientists didn’t have a good sense of how many tiger cat species existed. These small cats live in the tropical regions of the Americas and tend to look alike, Lescroart says.
paras.zh: 莱斯科罗特和他的同事并没有打算发现一个新物种。他们想要解开猫科动物谱系的一个分支。到目前为止，科学家们还不清楚存在多少种虎猫。莱斯科罗特说，这些小型猫科动物生活在美洲的热带地区，而且外表往往很相似。

paras.en: The researchers analyzed the genetics of 38 species of the Leopardus genus, which includes tiger cats as well as more widely known animals like the ocelot. They expected to find two, three or even four distinct species of tiger cat. Instead, Lescroart and his colleagues’ analyses pointed to five separate species, including one that scientists had never before described: L. tilcayo.
paras.zh: 研究人员分析了豹属 38 个物种的遗传学，其中包括虎猫以及豹猫等更广为人知的动物。他们期望找到两种、三种甚至四种不同种类的虎猫。相反，莱斯科罗特和他的同事的分析指出了五个不同的物种，其中包括科学家以前从未描述过的一种：L. tilcayo。

paras.en: The new species is based on two specimens: a female that was treated briefly for injuries at a sanctuary in Bolivia and released to the wild and a male that still lives at the sanctuary. His name is Tigrino. Lescroart’s colleague, Paola Nogales-Ascarrunz, met Tigrino at the sanctuary and noticed that he looked a little different from the cats she expected to see in the region. Nogales-Ascarrunz, a cat conservationist and National Geographic Explorer, genetically tested Tigrino and then connected with Lescroart’s team to share data.
paras.zh: 这个新物种基于两个标本：一个是在玻利维亚的保护区因受伤接受短暂治疗并被释放到野外的雌性，另一个是仍然生活在保护区的雄性。他的名字叫蒂格里诺。莱斯科罗特的同事保拉·诺加莱斯-阿斯卡伦兹 (Paola Nogales-Ascarrunz) 在保护区见到了蒂格里诺，并注意到它看起来与她预计在该地区看到的猫有些不同。诺加莱斯-阿斯卡伦兹 (Nogales-Ascarrunz) 是一名猫科动物保护主义者和国家地理探险家，他对 Tigrino 进行了基因测试，然后与 Lescroart 的团队联系以共享数据。

paras.en: The researchers’ work suggests that there’s diversity hiding even among well-studied animals like cats. “I don’t know if you’ll have to wait another 100 years for a new species,” Lescroart says. Though at the moment, the team doesn’t have any other cryptic kitties on the radar.
paras.zh: 研究人员的工作表明，即使在猫等经过充分研究的动物中也隐藏着多样性。 “我不知道是否还要再等 100 年才能出现新物种，”莱斯科罗特说。不过目前，该团队的雷达上还没有发现任何其他神秘的小猫。

articles.title: See the secret to DNA hookups
articles.author: Tina Hesman Saey

paras.en: DNA needs a little help to zip up its genes.
paras.zh: DNA 需要一点帮助来压缩它的基因。

paras.en: In a first, scientists have visualized how pieces of DNA pair up. Computer simulations further reveal that charged metal ions help twin double helices align, researchers report September 9 in Nucleic Acids Research.
paras.zh: 科学家们首先直观地了解了 DNA 片段如何配对。研究人员于 9 月 9 日在《核酸研究》上发表报告称，计算机模拟进一步表明，带电金属离子有助于双螺旋对齐。

paras.en: The work adds insight to the process in which cells pair up chromosomes before divvying DNA into eggs or sperm. Matching the chromosomes allows them to exchange information and keeps them from going astray, much like how folding socks keeps pairs together.
paras.zh: 这项工作增加了人们对细胞在将 DNA 分配到卵子或精子之前配对染色体的过程的了解。染色体匹配使它们能够交换信息并防止它们误入歧途，就像折叠袜子如何将配对保持在一起一样。

paras.en: But it’s not so easy to bring two DNA double helices together. The strands have a negative electrical charge and repel each other. Researchers previously hypothesized that positively charged ions could facilitate zipping the twisting strands of DNA together.
paras.zh: 但将两个 DNA 双螺旋连接在一起并不容易。这些股线带有负电荷并相互排斥。研究人员此前假设，带正电的离子可以促进 DNA 的扭曲链聚集在一起。

paras.en: Scientists at the University of Sheffield in England used atomic force microscopy to visualize short strands of DNA pairing up. The specialized microscope technique works like a record player, says microscopist Thomas Catley. A very sharp-tipped needle is dragged across a surface containing molecules the researchers want to examine. “We detect how that tip moves, and we turn that into an image signal, basically the same way that you get sound from a record player,” he says.
paras.zh: 英国谢菲尔德大学的科学家使用原子力显微镜观察短链 DNA 配对。显微镜学家托马斯·卡特利 (Thomas Catley) 表示，这种专门的显微镜技术就像电唱机一样工作。将一根非常锋利的针头拖过含有研究人员想要检查的分子的表面。 “我们检测尖端如何移动，然后将其转化为图像信号，基本上与从电唱机获取声音的方式相同，”他说。

paras.en: The zipped DNA strands look like twisted pieces of yarn with their grooves nestling together.
paras.zh: 拉上拉链的 DNA 链看起来就像扭曲的纱线，它们的凹槽依偎在一起。

paras.en: An atomic force microscope image shows identical DNA double helices pairing up. A zoomed in look (box, upper left) shows two double strands of DNA nestling together. Pink stars and green triangles indicate the alternating arrangement of grooves where the attraction between positively charged metal ions and negatively charged DNA holds the helices together.
paras.zh: 原子力显微镜图像显示相同的 DNA 双螺旋配对。放大后的图像（左上方框）显示两条 DNA 双链依偎在一起。粉色星星和绿色三角形表示凹槽的交替排列，其中带正电的金属离子和带负电的 DNA 之间的吸引力将螺旋固定在一起。

paras.en: Agnes Noy, a computational biophysicist at the University of York in England, was so taken with the images that she and colleagues did computer simulations to explain the mechanism. Positively charged metal ions nestle in the grooves of the DNA’s spiral staircases. That’s where information-carrying bases sit. The ions form bridges with the negatively charged ridges of the DNA backbone.
paras.zh: 英国约克大学的计算生物物理学家艾格尼丝·诺伊（Agnes Noy）对这些图像非常着迷，以至于她和同事进行了计算机模拟来解释这一机制。带正电的金属离子坐落在 DNA 螺旋楼梯的凹槽中。这就是信息承载基地所在的地方。这些离子与 DNA 主链带负电的脊形成桥。

paras.en: The DNA strands are staggered so that positive and negative charges alternate, the simulations suggest. The opposite charges attract the strands to each other. Together the images and simulations confirm the DNA zipper model, the researchers say.
paras.zh: 模拟表明，DNA 链是交错的，因此正电荷和负电荷交替。相反的电荷将股线相互吸引。研究人员表示，图像和模拟共同证实了 DNA 拉链模型。

paras.en: This knowledge may help bioengineers make better folds in DNA origami structures used to deliver drugs and give a better understanding of biological processes, including what goes wrong in some cancers.
paras.zh: 这些知识可能有助于生物工程师更好地折叠用于输送药物的 DNA 折纸结构，并更好地了解生物过程，包括某些癌症中出现的问题。

articles.title: These are the first feathers ever found in fossilized dinosaur poop
articles.author: Erin Garcia de Jesús

paras.en: Exquisitely preserved feathers, the first ever found in fossilized dinosaur poop, are providing a peek into how some ancient birds lived — and possibly went extinct.
paras.zh: 保存完好的羽毛是在恐龙粪便化石中首次发现的，这让人们得以了解一些古代鸟类的生活方式——甚至可能已经灭绝。

paras.en: Dense bristles suggest some of the feathers could repel water, possibly as well as those of modern pelicans, researchers report September 10 in Current Biology. And their central shafts are filled with air pockets, a trait that in modern birds keeps plumage lightweight yet stiff enough for flight. “That’s something we’re seeing for the first time in the Age of the Dinosaurs,” says vertebrate paleontologist Jingmai O’Connor of the Field Museum of Natural History in Chicago.
paras.zh: 研究人员在 9 月 10 日的《当代生物学》杂志上报告称，浓密的刚毛表明某些羽毛可以防水，可能与现代鹈鹕的羽毛一样。它们的中心轴充满了气穴，这一特征使现代鸟类的羽毛保持轻质但又足够坚硬，适合飞行。 “这是我们在恐龙时代第一次看到的东西，”芝加哥菲尔德自然历史博物馆的脊椎动物古生物学家景迈·奥康纳说。

paras.en: The find also offers a clue that might explain why, among birds, there were winners and losers in the mass extinction that ended the dinosaurs’ reign about 66 million years ago. The ancestors of modern birds survived the asteroid-triggered event while many other types of birds, including the group these feathers came from, died out.
paras.zh: 这一发现还提供了一条线索，可以解释为什么在大约 6600 万年前结束恐龙统治的大灭绝中，鸟类中有赢家和输家。现代鸟类的祖先在小行星引发的事件中幸存下来，而许多其他类型的鸟类，包括这些羽毛的来源群体，都灭绝了。

paras.en: One of O’Connor’s colleagues unearthed the fossilized dung, or coprolite, in 2016 in Montana’s Hell Creek Formation. If it weren’t for a “lucky break” on the coprolite’s surface that put one feather on full display, her team might never have known it had feathers inside, O’Connor says.
paras.zh: 2016 年，奥康纳的一位同事在蒙大拿州的地狱溪地层中发现了粪便化石，即粪石。奥康纳说，如果不是粪化石表面的“幸运突破”使一根羽毛充分展示出来，她的团队可能永远不会知道里面有羽毛。

paras.en: The scientists used micro-CT scans to 3-D map the coprolite’s inner contents. Leg bones and fish scales suggest the bird was aquatic — a member of a group called hesperonithiforms — and that it had eaten shortly before its demise. And while some of the feathers resembled those of modern birds, others were more primitive and stringy, which could have made it difficult for the bird to maintain body heat.
paras.zh: 科学家们使用微型 CT 扫描来绘制粪化石内部内容物的 3D 地图。腿骨和鱼鳞表明，这种鸟是水生的，是一种名为橙石形目（hesperonithiforms）的类群的成员，而且它在死亡前不久就吃过东西。虽然有些羽毛与现代鸟类的羽毛相似，但另一些羽毛则更为原始且粘稠，这可能使鸟类难以保持体温。

paras.en: Poor insulation might explain why hesperonithiforms and their close kin didn’t survive the deep chill that followed the asteroid impact, O’Connor says. But researchers need more feathers from various bird species during that time period to test the hypothesis. And fossilized feathers are incredibly rare.
paras.zh: 奥康纳说，绝缘不良可能解释了为什么橙石类动物及其近亲无法在小行星撞击后的严寒中幸存下来。但研究人员需要该时期不同鸟类的更多羽毛来检验这一假设。羽毛化石非常罕见。

paras.en: Now that it’s clear poop can be an excellent guardian of plumage, O’Connor says, “people should start looking.”
paras.zh: 奥康纳说，现在很明显粪便可以成为羽毛的优秀守护者，“人们应该开始寻找。”

articles.title: Revolutionary Feathered Dinosaur Discovery in China Suggests Flight Evolved Multiple Times
articles.author: Jess Cockerill

paras.en: An exquisitely preserved feathered raptor just discovered in north-eastern China could probably fly.
paras.zh: 刚在中国东北发现的一种保存完好的羽毛猛禽可能会飞。

paras.en: It's also somewhat disrupted the evolutionary path we thought birds took to get into the air.
paras.zh: 这也在一定程度上扰乱了我们认为鸟类飞向空中的进化路径。

paras.en: Norellraptor barsboldi, as the new dinosaur has been named, is a microraptor, which means it's a small dinosaur with feathers and wings.
paras.zh: 新恐龙被命名为诺雷盗龙巴氏恐龙（Norellraptor Barsboldi），它是一种小盗龙，这意味着它是一种长有羽毛和翅膀的小型恐龙。

paras.en: It's also a member of the wider group Paraves, which includes a range of theropod dinosaurs, including some that are still thriving today: birds.
paras.zh: 它也是更广泛的帕拉韦斯恐龙群体的成员，该群体包括一系列兽脚亚目恐龙，其中包括一些至今仍然繁衍生息的鸟类：鸟类。

paras.en: And, like its living relatives, Norellraptor could probably fly.
paras.zh: 而且，就像它活着的亲戚一样，诺瑞盗龙可能会飞。

paras.en: But close analysis of this remarkably detailed fossil suggests the evolutionary path to flight may be far more forked than we thought.
paras.zh: 但对这块非常详细的化石的仔细分析表明，飞行的进化路径可能比我们想象的更加复杂。

paras.en: Norellraptor is described in a new paper by paleontologist Xuri Wang of the Chinese Academy of Geological Sciences and his colleagues. The paper is published in Nature Communications.
paras.zh: 中国地质科学院古生物学家王旭日及其同事在一篇新论文中描述了诺雷尔盗龙。该论文发表在《自然通讯》上。

paras.en: The microraptor's body is 57 centimeters long (just over 22 inches), and based on its bones, the researchers think it hadn't quite finished growing at the time of its death.
paras.zh: 小盗龙的身体长 57 厘米（略高于 22 英寸），根据其骨骼，研究人员认为它在死亡时尚未完全生长。

paras.en: Its feathers are much less well-preserved than its bones, but from what the researchers could see, its forelimbs and tail seem to have been festooned with flight-related plumage, while other parts of its body were covered in straight, simple feathers.
paras.zh: 它的羽毛比它的骨头保存得要差得多，但从研究人员的观察来看，它的前肢和尾巴似乎装饰着与飞行有关的羽毛，而身体的其他部分则覆盖着直而简单的羽毛。

paras.en: Certain features in this Norellraptor's bones, and a close look at where it sits in the Paraves family tree has led the researchers to question what we know about how flight evolved within Paraves.
paras.zh: 这只 Norellraptor 骨骼的某些特征，以及对它在 Paraves 家谱中的位置的仔细观察，让研究人员质疑我们对 Paraves 飞行是如何进化的了解。

paras.en: The fact that both microraptors and birds evolved the ability to fly doesn't necessarily mean they inherited the trait from the same ancestor.
paras.zh: 小盗龙和鸟类都进化出了飞行能力的事实并不一定意味着它们继承了同一祖先的特征。

paras.en: Norellraptor's current position in the Paraves family tree suggests flight may have actually arisen at least twice, independently.
paras.zh: 诺雷尔猛禽目前在帕拉韦斯家谱中的位置表明，飞行实际上可能至少独立地出现过两次。

paras.en: The steps it followed to reach the skies seem to be quite different from those taken by birds.
paras.zh: 它到达天空的步骤似乎与鸟类所采取的步骤截然不同。

paras.en: Another bit of evidence is that the development of the dinosaur's forearm, or wing, seems to have stopped quite early in its life, which is the opposite of what we see in modern, flying birds.
paras.zh: 另一个证据是，恐龙的前臂或翅膀的发育似乎在其生命的早期就停止了，这与我们在现代飞鸟中看到的相反。

paras.en: "The sequences of flight-related novelties reconstructed along the two lineages differ consistently," Wang and team write.
paras.zh: “沿着两个谱系重建的与飞行相关的新奇事物的序列始终不同，”王和团队写道。

paras.en: "Combined with histological evidence which might indicate a peculiar limb growth model in Microraptorinae, these results dismiss a shared developmental pattern driving the evolution of the flying dinosaurs and support multiple and independent selective regimes at the origin of the winged taxa in Paraves."
paras.zh: “结合可能表明小盗龙亚科独特的肢体生长模型的组织学证据，这些结果驳回了驱动飞行恐龙进化的共同发育模式，并支持帕拉韦斯有翼类群起源的多个独立的选择机制。”

paras.en: In other words, there might have been some convergent evolution going on in the Paraves family.
paras.zh: 换句话说，帕拉维斯家族可能正在发生一些趋同进化。

paras.en: That's when two separate evolutionary groups reach a similar outcome via a totally different route. Think whales and fishes: both can swim using fins, but they arrived at that body plan from totally different paths.
paras.zh: 那时两个不同的进化群体通过完全不同的路线达到了相似的结果。想想鲸鱼和鱼类：两者都可以用鳍游泳，但它们从完全不同的路径达到了身体计划。

paras.en: Still, paleontologists can't rely on just one fossil to rewrite evolutionary history.
paras.zh: 尽管如此，古生物学家不能仅依靠一块化石来改写进化历史。

paras.en: A lot more evidence will be needed before scientists are convinced that birds and microraptors did indeed evolve flight entirely independently.
paras.zh: 在科学家确信鸟类和小盗龙确实完全独立地进化出飞行能力之前，还需要更多的证据。

paras.en: "Microraptorines have been advocated as models for investigating the origin and evolution of the avian flight," the authors note.
paras.zh: “小盗龙被提倡作为研究鸟类飞行起源和进化的模型，”作者指出。

paras.en: "Yet, the evolutionary relationships between the flight apparatus of birds and the purported aerial adaptations of the microraptorines are controversial from both functional and phylogenetic perspectives."
paras.zh: “然而，从功能和系统发育的角度来看，鸟类的飞行装置和所谓的小盗龙的空中适应之间的进化关系都存在争议。”

paras.en: The research has been published in Nature Communications.
paras.zh: 该研究已发表在《自然通讯》上。

articles.title: Physicists Find a Superconductor That 'Breaks' The Symmetry of Time – A First For Its Kind
articles.author: Ivan Farkas

paras.en: Under certain conditions – such as bone-brittling temperatures lower than that of deep space – superconductors can conduct electricity without resistance and resultant energy loss.
paras.zh: 在某些条件下——例如比深空温度低的骨头脆化温度——超导体可以在没有电阻和能量损失的情况下导电。

paras.en: Though they vary in their chemical composition, operational temperature ranges, and magnetic properties, superconductors come in two groupings.
paras.zh: 尽管超导体的化学成分、工作温度范围和磁性各不相同，但它们分为两类。

paras.en: First, conventional and unconventional superconductors differ in how their electrons become entangled in tandems called Cooper pairs, an identity-sharing state that allows them to gracefully glide through the atomic jumble of their materials to facilitate uninterrupted electric flow.
paras.zh: 首先，传统和非常规超导体的不同之处在于它们的电子如何以库珀对的方式纠缠在一起，这是一种身份共享状态，使它们能够优雅地滑过其材料的原子杂乱，以促进不间断的电流。

paras.en: Secondly, type I and type II superconductors respond differently to magnetic fields, with distinct types of thresholds at which they abruptly stop operating as superconductors and start acting like regular conductors.
paras.zh: 其次，I 型和 II 型超导体对磁场的响应不同，具有不同类型的阈值，在阈值处它们会突然停止作为超导体运行并开始像常规导体一样运行。

paras.en: Unconventional and type II varieties are generally considered more exotic; the Lamborghinis of their domain, pushing physical boundaries because they require bespoke engineering.
paras.zh: 非常规和 II 类品种通常被认为更具异国情调；他们领域的兰博基尼，突破物理界限，因为它们需要定制工程。

paras.en: They may also be more suited as workhorses used in technologies like MRIs, much as Lamborghinis used to be tractors.
paras.zh: 它们也可能更适合作为核磁共振等技术中使用的主力，就像兰博基尼曾经是拖拉机一样。

paras.en: But perhaps no longer. Because, for the first time, physicists have created a type I superconductor material that can seemingly break the mathematical symmetry of time – a hallmark of unconventional, type II superconductors.
paras.zh: 但也许不再了。因为，物理学家首次创造了一种 I 型超导材料，它似乎可以打破时间的数学对称性——这是非传统 II 型超导体的标志。

paras.en: Known as time-reversal symmetry, this comprises a curious observation that most of the laws of physics work equally well whether time mathematically flows forward or backward
paras.zh: 这被称为时间反转对称性，其中包含一个奇怪的观察结果，即无论时间在数学上向前或向后流动，大多数物理定律都同样有效

paras.en: In a study recently published in Physical Review Letters, an international team of physicists led by the Indian Institute of Science Education and Research (IISER) Bhopal analyzed and described this material's unique electrical and quantum qualities, suggesting that it may eventually improve quantum computing designs.
paras.zh: 在最近发表在《物理评论快报》上的一项研究中，由印度科学教育与研究学院 (IISER) 博帕尔领导的国际物理学家团队分析并描述了这种材料独特的电学和量子特性，表明它最终可能会改善量子计算设计。

paras.en: The researchers synthesized single crystals of a material called ytterbium diantimonide (YbSb2) and used X-rays to determine its chemical purity and complex crystal structure – a structure common in conventional and unconventional superconductors because it allows quantum behaviors to emerge.
paras.zh: 研究人员合成了一种名为二锑化镱 (YbSb2) 的材料的单晶，并使用 X 射线确定其化学纯度和复杂的晶体结构——这是传统和非常规超导体中常见的结构，因为它允许量子行为的出现。

paras.en: They determined that its electrical resistance dropped to zero and it abruptly became superconducting at a temperature of around -272 degrees Celsius (-457.6 degrees Fahrenheit), which is just a smidge above absolute zero (-273.15 degrees Celsius).
paras.zh: 他们确定其电阻降至零，并在 -272 摄氏度（-457.6 华氏度）左右的温度下突然变得超导，该温度仅略高于绝对零（-273.15 摄氏度）。

paras.en: Combined with specific heat measurements of how its electrons respond to heat, the researchers confirmed that their material exhibited type I superconducting properties.
paras.zh: 结合电子对热反应的比热测量，研究人员证实他们的材料表现出 I 型超导特性。

paras.en: This measure also helped confirm its "fully gapped" state, meaning it features an energy barrier that makes it harder to disentangle its paired electrons, and therefore knock it out of a superconducting state.
paras.zh: 这项措施还有助于确认其“完全带隙”状态，这意味着它具有能垒，使其更难解开成对电子，从而使其脱离超导状态。

paras.en: The researchers also used two types of muon spin spectroscopy, a quantum probing technique that reveals the magnetic fields inside a material by zapping it with muons, or fundamental subatomic particles that act like little bar magnets.
paras.zh: 研究人员还使用了两种类型的μ子自旋光谱，这是一种量子探测技术，通过用μ子或像小条形磁铁一样的基本亚原子粒子来探测材料内部的磁场。

paras.en: When they did so without applying an external magnetic field, they revealed that, once the material entered the superconducting phase, tiny internal magnetic fields spontaneously appeared within it.
paras.zh: 当他们在不施加外部磁场的情况下这样做时，他们发现，一旦材料进入超导相，微小的内部磁场就会自发地出现在其中。

paras.en: This provided the key evidence that YbSb2 could break time-reversal symmetry, since magnetic fields reverse their direction when time is mathematically reversed – if they didn't, they would preserve, rather than break, this curious property of time.
paras.zh: 这提供了关键证据，证明 YbSb2 可以打破时间反转对称性，因为当时间在数学上反转时，磁场会反转其方向 - 如果它们不这样做，它们将保留而不是破坏时间的这种奇怪特性。

paras.en: In another version of this quantum probing technique, the researchers applied external magnetic fields while beaming the material with muons.
paras.zh: 在这种量子探测技术的另一个版本中，研究人员在用μ介子发射材料的同时施加外部磁场。

paras.en: Additionally, when in a bulk superconducting state, the electrons in YbSb2 do not pair up in a traditional way.
paras.zh: 此外，当处于体超导状态时，YbSb2 中的电子不会以传统方式配对。

paras.en: Instead, they come together in an unconventional "spin triplet," which is a Cooper pair but called a triplet due to the possible combinations of the electrons' spins.
paras.zh: 相反，它们以非常规的“自旋三重态”聚集在一起，这是库珀对，但由于电子自旋的可能组合而被称为三重态。

paras.en: Importantly, this is more mouth-twistingly called an "internally antisymmetric non-unitary triplet (INT) state," so it displays a net magnetic moment – its magnetic forces do not cancel out.
paras.zh: 重要的是，这更绕口的称为“内部反对称非酉三重态（INT）态”，因此它显示出净磁矩——它的磁力不会抵消。

paras.en: This pairing allows YbSb2 to break the time-reversal symmetry on its own, without requiring an external magnetic field to do so.
paras.zh: 这种配对使得 YbSb2 能够自行打破时间反转对称性，而不需要外部磁场来做到这一点。

paras.en: To find out how triplets form, the researchers modeled their material based on fundamental physical qualities, revealing that each of the paired electrons comes from different energy orbitals.
paras.zh: 为了弄清楚三重态是如何形成的，研究人员根据基本物理特性对材料进行了建模，揭示了每个成对电子都来自不同的能量轨道。

paras.en: As a result, its combined properties may make YbSb2 able to host "gapless Majorana surface modes," which is not a top-selling Zelda game.
paras.zh: 因此，它的综合特性可能使 YbSb2 能够承载“无间隙马约拉纳表面模式”，这不是最畅销的塞尔达游戏。

paras.en: It means that, at low temperatures, while its bulk acts like a superconductor through which electrons flow unimpeded, its surface may manifest Majorana modes, or quantum excitations that act as their own antiparticles. (Possibly comparable to a delicious Red Vine, which transmits air through its bulk and sugar through its edges)
paras.zh: 这意味着，在低温下，虽然它的体积就像一个超导体，电子可以畅通无阻地流过，但它的表面可能会表现出马约拉纳模式，或者充当它们自己的反粒子的量子激发。 （可能类似于美味的红藤，它通过其体积传输空气，通过其边缘传输糖分）

paras.en: This could represent more than a theoretical breakthrough.
paras.zh: 这不仅仅代表了理论上的突破。

paras.en: Such "topological quantum materials" may be better able to protect quantum information by making it less vulnerable to external conditions like heat or electromagnetic noise – sources of interference that knock quantum systems out of their entangled (and therefore useful) states and relegate them to the computing powers of, well, regular computers.
paras.zh: 这种“拓扑量子材料”可能能够更好地保护量子信息，使其不易受到热或电磁噪声等外部条件的影响，这些干扰源会将量子系统从纠缠（因此有用）状态中剔除，并将其降级为普通计算机的计算能力。

paras.en: The research has been published in Physical Review Letters.
paras.zh: 该研究已发表在《物理评论快报》上。

articles.title: A Hidden Compound in 'Healthy' Plant-Based Foods May Be Fueling Gut Inflammation
articles.author: David Nield

paras.en: Some of the healthiest plant-based foods on the menu – including spinach, beetroot, rhubarb, almonds, and sweet potatoes – could be linked to inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), based on a new study.
paras.zh: 一项新的研究表明，菜单上一些最健康的植物性食物——包括菠菜、甜菜根、大黄、杏仁和红薯——可能与炎症性肠病（IBD）有关。

paras.en: The study comes from a team led by researchers from the University of North Carolina, and focuses on a natural compound found in all plant-based foods, called oxalate.
paras.zh: 这项研究来自北卡罗来纳大学研究人员领导的一个团队，重点关注所有植物性食品中发现的一种天然化合物，称为草酸盐。

paras.en: While oxalate doesn't have much use in the human body, it's also not inherently harmful – we just get rid of most of it as waste. But this latest research indicates that in some people, problems processing the compound properly may lead to gut issues.
paras.zh: 虽然草酸盐对人体没有多大用处，但它本质上也不是有害的——我们只是将其中大部分作为废物处理掉。但这项最新研究表明，对于某些人来说，正确处理这种化合物的问题可能会导致肠道问题。

paras.en: Part of the study, published in Cellular and Molecular Gastroenterology and Hepatology, measured the level of oxalate in a person's diet against what showed up in their stools. Two different analysis methods were used across a total of 46 participants, including some with Crohn's disease (CD), one of the two main IBD sub-types.
paras.zh: 该研究的一部分发表在《细胞和分子胃肠病学和肝病学》上，测量了一个人饮食中的草酸水平与粪便中的草酸水平。对总共 46 名参与者使用了两种不同的分析方法，其中包括一些患有克罗恩病 (CD) 的患者，克罗恩病是 IBD 的两种主要亚型之一。

paras.en: "For the first time, we observed that IBD patients and healthy controls were eating similar amounts of plant-based foods yet CD patients still had more oxalate in their stool," says gastrointestinal biologist Anna Salvador, from the University of North Carolina.
paras.zh: 北卡罗来纳大学胃肠道生物学家安娜·萨尔瓦多 (Anna Salvador) 表示：“我们首次观察到，炎症性肠病 (IBD) 患者和健康对照者摄入的植物性食品数量相似，但克罗恩病 (CD) 患者的粪便中草酸含量仍然较高。”

paras.en: "That told us this isn't just about what patients eat. Something is fundamentally different about how their gut handles oxalate."
paras.zh: “这告诉我们，这不仅仅是患者吃什么的问题。他们的肠道处理草酸盐的方式有根本的不同。”

paras.en: The researchers also looked at transporter proteins called SLC26A2 and SLC26A3, which absorb oxalate from the gut. In several hundred tissue samples taken from people with CD, ulcerative colitis (the other main IBD sub-type), and healthy controls, genes producing these proteins were found to be less active in the IBD samples.
paras.zh: 研究人员还研究了名为 SLC26A2 和 SLC26A3 的转运蛋白，它们从肠道吸收草酸盐。在取自 CD、溃疡性结肠炎（IBD 的另一种主要亚型）患者和健康对照者的数百个组织样本中，发现产生这些蛋白质的基因在 IBD 样本中活性较低。

paras.en: Another aspect of the study involved tests on mice with deliberately inflamed guts (to resemble IBD). These experiments showed that animals fed extra oxalate fared worse by several measures: they lost more weight, developed a greater level of intestinal inflammation for longer, and were less likely to survive.
paras.zh: 该研究的另一个方面涉及对肠道故意发炎（类似于炎症性肠病）的小鼠进行测试。这些实验表明，从几个方面来看，喂食额外草酸盐的动物表现更差：它们体重减轻更多，肠道炎症程度更高，持续时间更长，并且存活的可能性更小。

paras.en: The researchers even had time to examine the reaction of mouse immune cells to oxalate in the lab. The compound increased the inflammatory response, suggesting it's an immune system reaction rather than direct damage that links oxalate and IBD.
paras.zh: 研究人员甚至有时间在实验室中检查小鼠免疫细胞对草酸盐的反应。该化合物增加了炎症反应，表明草酸盐和炎症性肠病之间存在联系，这是一种免疫系统反应，而不是直接损伤。

paras.en: "These findings identify dietary oxalate as a potentially modifiable factor in intestinal inflammation and underscore the need to consider variation in dietary exposures and oxalate metabolism in inflammatory bowel diseases," write the researchers in their published paper.
paras.zh: 研究人员在发表的论文中写道：“这些发现确定膳食草酸盐是肠道炎症的一个潜在可改变因素，并强调需要考虑炎症性肠病中饮食暴露和草酸盐代谢的变化。”

paras.en: Possible next steps for the research include trying to target the transporter proteins SLC26A2 and SLC26A3 as a route to making sure that oxalate is effectively cleared out from the gut, rather than building up to harmful levels.
paras.zh: 该研究的下一步可能包括尝试以转运蛋白 SLC26A2 和 SLC26A3 为目标，以确保草酸从肠道中有效清除，而不是累积到有害水平。

paras.en: Along those lines, the researchers also looked at a third oxalate transporter protein, SLC26A6. In an examination of 131 people with Crohn's disease, a less active SLC26A6 gene was linked with a more severe type of the condition.
paras.zh: 沿着这些思路，研究人员还研究了第三种草酸转运蛋白 SLC26A6。在对 131 名克罗恩病患者进行的检查中，发现活性较低的 SLC26A6 基因与更严重的克罗恩病类型有关。

paras.en: "For patients living with Crohn's disease or ulcerative colitis, this research opens a genuinely new therapeutic angle," says geneticist Shehzad Sheikh, from the University of North Carolina. "One that connects the food on their plate to the inflammation in their gut."
paras.zh: “对于患有克罗恩病或溃疡性结肠炎的患者来说，这项研究开辟了一个真正新的治疗角度，”北卡罗来纳大学的遗传学家 Shehzad Sheikh 说。 “一种将盘子里的食物与肠道炎症联系起来的方法。”

paras.en: It's well accepted that diet plays a role in IBD, alongside several other key factors, and the oxalate found in plant-based foods may be a part of that. The researchers aren't suggesting that these foods should be cut out of anyone's diet, but that moderating oxalate intake could be of benefit.
paras.zh: 人们普遍认为，饮食以及其他几个关键因素在 IBD 中发挥着重要作用，而植物性食品中发现的草酸盐可能是其中的一部分。研究人员并不是建议任何人的饮食中都应去除这些食物，但适量摄入草酸可能会有所帮助。

paras.en: Further down the line, it's possible that extra supplements – perhaps promoting bacteria that help the body get rid of oxalate – could be part of IBD treatment options. Studies with larger groups of participants should tell us more about the potential mechanisms at play, and identify those who might be more sensitive to oxalate.
paras.zh: 进一步来说，额外的补充剂——或许促进细菌生长，帮助身体清除草酸盐——可能成为炎症性肠病治疗方案的一部分。对更多参与者进行的研究应该告诉我们更多有关潜在机制的信息，并确定那些可能对草酸盐更敏感的人。

paras.en: "Diet is one of the most powerful, modifiable levers we have in medicine, and this study gives us a molecular framework to start using it more precisely," says Sheikh.
paras.zh: “饮食是我们在医学上最强大、最可修改的杠杆之一，这项研究为我们提供了一个分子框架，可以开始更精确地使用它，”谢赫说。

paras.en: The research has been published in Cellular and Molecular Gastroenterology and Hepatology.
paras.zh: 该研究已发表在《细胞与分子胃肠病学》和《肝病学》杂志上。

articles.title: 1 in 13 adults under 30 already had hidden artery plaque

paras.en: 1 in 13 adults under 30 already had hidden artery plaque
paras.zh: 30 岁以下的成年人中，每 13 人中就有 1 人已有隐藏的动脉斑块

paras.en: A huge study found silent artery-clogging disease in more than half of apparently healthy adults, including surprisingly young people.
paras.zh: 一项大型研究发现，超过一半表面健康的成年人患有无症状的动脉阻塞疾病，其中包括令人惊讶的年轻人。

paras.en: - Centro Nacional de Investigaciones Cardiovasculares Carlos III (F.S.P.)
paras.zh: - 卡洛斯三世国家心血管研究中心 (F.S.P.)

paras.en: - More than half of 16,000 apparently healthy adults had signs of atherosclerosis, with arterial plaques already detectable in about 1 in 13 people ages 18 to 29. Researchers say directly imaging the arteries could reveal hidden cardiovascular disease years or even decades before symptoms appear.
paras.zh: - 16,000 名表面健康的成年人中，超过一半有动脉粥样硬化的迹象，在 18 至 29 岁的人中，大约三分之一的人已经检测到动脉斑块。研究人员表示，直接对动脉进行成像可以在症状出现前数年甚至数十年发现隐藏的心血管疾病。

paras.en: Atherosclerosis, the gradual buildup of plaque inside arteries that drives most cardiovascular disease, can begin many years before a person notices any symptoms. Now, a large international study suggests that this hidden disease is already present in some young adults who otherwise appear healthy, and that it is considerably more widespread than previously recognized.
paras.zh: 动脉粥样硬化是动脉内斑块逐渐积聚的结果，它会导致大多数心血管疾病，它可能在人们注意到任何症状之前很多年就开始出现。现在，一项大型国际研究表明，这种隐藏的疾病已经存在于一些原本健康的年轻人身上，而且其传播范围比之前认识的要广泛得多。

paras.en: The research was led by Professor Henning Bundgaard, Professor of Cardiology at Rigshospitalet in Copenhagen, Denmark, and Dr. Borja Ibáñez, Scientific Director of the Centro Nacional de Investigaciones Cardiovasculares Carlos III, CNIC, cardiologist at Hospital Universitario Fundación Jiménez Díaz and a group leader at CIBERCV.
paras.zh: 该研究由丹麦哥本哈根 Rigshospitalet 心脏病学教授 Henning Bundgaard 教授和卡洛斯三世国家心血管研究中心科学主任、CNIC、希门尼斯·迪亚斯大学基金会医院心脏病专家、CIBERCV 小组组长 Borja Ibáñez 博士领导。

paras.en: Among more than 16,000 participants with no symptoms or previous cardiovascular disease diagnosis, researchers detected atherosclerotic plaques in 57.1%. The findings were presented in a Hot Line session at ESC Congress 2026 and published at the same time in The New England Journal of Medicine.
paras.zh: 在 16,000 多名没有症状或既往没有心血管疾病诊断的参与者中，研究人员检测到 57.1% 的人患有动脉粥样硬化斑块。研究结果在 2026 年 ESC 大会的热线会议上发表，并同时发表在《新英格兰医学杂志》上。

paras.en: Mapping Hidden Atherosclerosis Across Adult Life
paras.zh: 绘制成人生活中隐藏的动脉粥样硬化

paras.en: The findings come from the first phase of REACT, one of the largest efforts yet to examine how silent atherosclerosis develops throughout adulthood. The international project is funded by the Novo Nordisk Foundation and carried out through a collaboration involving Rigshospitalet, other Danish hospitals and CNIC in Spain.
paras.zh: 这些发现来自 REACT 的第一阶段，这是迄今为止为研究无症状动脉粥样硬化在整个成年期如何发展而进行的最大努力之一。该国际项目由诺和诺德基金会资助，并通过 Rigshospitalet、其他丹麦医院和西班牙 CNIC 的合作开展。

paras.en: Professor Bundgaard explains that "the vision of REACT is to transform primary cardiovascular prevention through a precision medicine approach based on the early identification of atherosclerosis."
paras.zh: Bundgaard 教授解释说，“REACT 的愿景是通过基于动脉粥样硬化早期识别的精准医学方法来改变心血管疾病的初级预防。”

paras.en: The Novo Nordisk Foundation awarded up to EUR 23 million to support the initiative's first phase.
paras.zh: 诺和诺德基金会拨款高达 2300 万欧元来支持该计划的第一阶段。

paras.en: Atherosclerosis is the primary underlying cause of cardiovascular disease, which can eventually appear as a heart attack, stroke or sudden death. Having arterial plaque does not mean that a person will inevitably develop symptomatic disease. However, cardiovascular disease kills nearly 20 million people around the world each year, with atherosclerosis responsible for most of those deaths.
paras.zh: 动脉粥样硬化是心血管疾病的主要原因，最终可能表现为心脏病发作、中风或猝死。拥有动脉斑块并不意味着一个人将不可避免地出现症状性疾病。然而，全世界每年有近 2000 万人死于心血管疾病，其中大部分死亡是由动脉粥样硬化引起的。

paras.en: One of the challenges is that the disease can develop quietly for decades. Plaque may continue accumulating inside the arteries without producing any obvious warning signs.
paras.zh: 挑战之一是这种疾病可以悄然发展数十年。斑块可能会继续在动脉内积聚，而不会产生任何明显的警告信号。

paras.en: Looking for Disease Instead of Estimating Risk
paras.zh: 寻找疾病而不是估计风险

paras.en: Professor Ibáñez stated that "the REACT study is based on a simple but revolutionary idea: moving from the current model, which estimates the probability of cardiovascular disease on the basis of traditional risk factors such as blood pressure, cholesterol and smoking, towards a new paradigm in which the disease is detected directly through imaging before it causes symptoms. In this model, preventive interventions and the treatment of risk factors could be guided by the actual presence of silent atherosclerosis rather than relying solely on an indirect estimate of risk. The first step in this ambitious endeavour was to determine the actual prevalence of silent atherosclerosis in all three major vascular territories and across the entire adult lifespan, something that we are reporting now."
paras.zh: Ibáñez教授表示，“REACT研究基于一个简单但革命性的想法：从当前的模型（根据血压、胆固醇和吸烟等传统风险因素估计心血管疾病的概率）转向一种新的范式，在疾病引起症状之前通过成像直接检测到疾病。在这个模型中，预防性干预和风险因素的治疗可以通过无症状动脉粥样硬化的实际存在来指导，而不是仅仅依赖于对风险的间接估计。这一雄心勃勃的努力的第一步是以确定所有三个主要血管区域和整个成人寿命中无症状动脉粥样硬化的实际患病率，这是我们现在正在报告的内容。”

paras.en: In other words, rather than relying only on factors such as cholesterol, smoking and blood pressure to calculate someone's future cardiovascular risk, the researchers want to determine whether plaque is already present.
paras.zh: 换句话说，研究人员希望确定斑块是否已经存在，而不是仅仅依靠胆固醇、吸烟和血压等因素来计算某人未来的心血管风险。

paras.en: REACT is expected to span eight years and two phases. Phase 1 (REACT-DETECT) began in 2024 and, if funding is granted, Phase 2 (REACT-PROTECT) is planned to run from 2027 through 2032.
paras.zh: REACT预计将持续八年，分两个阶段。第一阶段 (REACT-DETECT) 于 2024 年开始，如果获得资金，第二阶段 (REACT-PROTECT) 计划于 2027 年至 2032 年运行。

paras.en: The current results come from Phase 1, which researchers say provides the most comprehensive picture yet of where silent atherosclerosis appears in the body, how common it is at different ages, and how its prevalence differs between women and men.
paras.zh: 目前的结果来自第一阶段，研究人员表示，该结果提供了迄今为止最全面的图片，显示了无症状动脉粥样硬化在体内出现的位置、它在不同年龄段的常见程度以及女性和男性之间的患病率有何不同。

paras.en: Atherosclerosis Is Already Present in Young Adults
paras.zh: 动脉粥样硬化已经存在于年轻人中

paras.en: For the first phase, researchers enrolled 16,808 people ages 18 to 70 in Denmark and Spain. None had a known history of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease.
paras.zh: 在第一阶段，研究人员在丹麦和西班牙招募了 16,808 名 18 岁至 70 岁的人。没有人有动脉粥样硬化性心血管疾病的已知病史。

paras.en: Every participant underwent advanced imaging designed to identify plaque in three major areas: the carotid arteries in the neck, the femoral arteries in the legs and the coronary arteries supplying the heart.
paras.zh: 每个参与者都接受了先进的成像技术，旨在识别三个主要区域的斑块：颈部的颈动脉、腿部的股动脉和供应心脏的冠状动脉。

paras.en: The researchers also examined cardiovascular risk factors and blood biomarkers, collected samples for omics studies and analyzed retinal images. Together, these measurements created one of the most extensive databases on atherosclerosis assembled to date.
paras.zh: 研究人员还检查了心血管危险因素和血液生物标志物，收集样本进行组学研究并分析视网膜图像。这些测量结果共同创建了迄今为止最广泛的动脉粥样硬化数据库之一。

paras.en: The scans showed that atherosclerosis can appear surprisingly early in adulthood. About 1 in 13 participants ages 18 to 29 had signs of the disease in at least one artery.
paras.zh: 扫描结果显示，动脉粥样硬化可能在成年早期就出现。年龄在 18 至 29 岁之间的参与者中，约有三分之一的人至少在一根动脉中出现这种疾病的迹象。

paras.en: The prevalence then climbed steadily with age. Among participants ages 60 to 70, about 9 in 10 had atherosclerosis.
paras.zh: 随着年龄的增长，患病率稳步上升。在 60 至 70 岁的参与者中，大约十分之九患有动脉粥样硬化。

paras.en: Ultrasound Could Offer a Simpler Way to Screen
paras.zh: 超声波可以提供更简单的筛查方法

paras.en: Another important pattern emerged from the imaging. Most participants who had atherosclerosis in their coronary arteries also showed plaque in the carotid or femoral arteries.
paras.zh: 成像中出现了另一个重要的模式。大多数冠状动脉患有动脉粥样硬化的参与者的颈动脉或股动脉也出现斑块。

paras.en: That overlap could have significant implications for future screening. Imaging the carotid and femoral arteries with ultrasound is easier, quicker and noninvasive compared with performing CT scans to examine the coronary arteries.
paras.zh: 这种重叠可能会对未来的筛查产生重大影响。与通过 CT 扫描检查冠状动脉相比，用超声对颈动脉和股动脉进行成像更容易、更快速且无创。

paras.en: "In the paradigm we propose, portable ultrasound devices usable by any healthcare professional will become the standard tool for atherosclerosis screening from the early stages of adult life," Dr. Ibáñez said.
paras.zh: “在我们提出的范例中，任何医疗保健专业人员都可以使用的便携式超声设备将成为成人早期阶段动脉粥样硬化筛查的标准工具，”伊巴涅斯博士说。

paras.en: The study also identified notable differences in how atherosclerosis appeared across the lifespan in men and women.
paras.zh: 该研究还发现男性和女性在一生中动脉粥样硬化的出现方式存在显着差异。

paras.en: Among men, prevalence began increasing at younger ages. Their overall pattern of atherosclerosis appeared about five to ten years ahead of the pattern seen in women.
paras.zh: 在男性中，患病率在年轻时就开始增加。他们的动脉粥样硬化总体模式比女性早大约五到十年。

paras.en: Women showed their sharpest rise between ages 40 and 60, a period that broadly overlaps with the menopausal transition.
paras.zh: 女性的发病率在 40 岁至 60 岁之间增长最快，这一时期与更年期过渡期大致重叠。

paras.en: The researchers say these differences underscore the need to investigate cardiovascular prevention strategies that account for both sex and stage of life.
paras.zh: 研究人员表示，这些差异强调了研究考虑性别和生命阶段的心血管预防策略的必要性。

paras.en: Traditional Risk Scores Miss Many Existing Cases
paras.zh: 传统风险评分遗漏了许多现有案例

paras.en: One of the study's most consequential findings involved conventional cardiovascular risk assessment.
paras.zh: 该研究最重要的发现之一涉及传统的心血管风险评估。

paras.en: Current methods, including risk scores such as SCORE2, identified only a small proportion of people who already had silent atherosclerosis. That suggests a person can appear to have relatively low cardiovascular risk according to traditional measures while plaque is already developing inside the arteries.
paras.zh: 目前的方法，包括 SCORE2 等风险评分，仅识别出一小部分已经患有无症状动脉粥样硬化的人。这表明，根据传统措施，当斑块已经在动脉内形成时，一个人的心血管风险似乎相对较低。

paras.en: According to Dr. Ibáñez, the findings point toward a potentially different approach to preventing cardiovascular disease.
paras.zh: 伊瓦涅斯博士表示，这些发现指出了预防心血管疾病的潜在不同方法。

paras.en: "For decades, we have estimated cardiovascular risk using factors such as age, blood pressure and cholesterol. This study shows that we can now go one step further and detect the disease directly before it causes a heart attack or stroke."
paras.zh: “几十年来，我们利用年龄、血压和胆固醇等因素来估计心血管风险。这项研究表明，我们现在可以更进一步，在疾病导致心脏病发作或中风之前直接检测到它。”

paras.en: He added: "The future of cardiovascular prevention must be more precise and personalized. If we identify atherosclerosis in its earliest stages, we will be able to intervene sooner, tailor treatment more effectively and reduce the burden of cardiovascular disease."
paras.zh: 他补充道：“未来的心血管预防必须更加精准和个性化。如果我们能在最早阶段发现动脉粥样硬化，我们将能够更快地进行干预，更有效地制定治疗方案，并减轻心血管疾病的负担。”

paras.en: Professor Bundgaard believes the findings could provide an opportunity to rethink how cardiovascular prevention is carried out.
paras.zh: 邦德加德教授认为，这些发现可能为重新思考如何进行心血管预防提供了机会。

paras.en: "Until now, preventive decisions have been based on an estimate of risk, but we did not know whether the disease was already present. REACT shows that atherosclerosis can be detected decades before clinical manifestations appear and provides the most comprehensive atlas of the evolution of the disease across adult life."
paras.zh: “到目前为止，预防决策都是基于对风险的估计，但我们不知道这种疾病是否已经存在。REACT 表明，动脉粥样硬化可以在临床表现出现之前几十年就被检测出来，并提供了该疾病在成人生活中演变的最全面的图谱。”

paras.en: Testing Whether Earlier Detection Improves Outcomes
paras.zh: 测试早期检测是否可以改善结果

paras.en: Professor Bundgaard added that the results create the scientific foundation needed to test whether this proposed preventive approach actually improves health outcomes.
paras.zh: Bundgaard 教授补充说，这些结果为测试这种提议的预防方法是否真正改善健康结果奠定了必要的科学基础。

paras.en: "Identifying and treating silent atherosclerosis as early as possible is essential to reducing the global burden of cardiovascular disease. Our results support prospective studies evaluating whether a preventive strategy guided by imaging, including the use of portable ultrasound, can improve current standards. If confirmed, this would bring precision medicine to the most common cardiovascular disease."
paras.zh: “尽早识别和治疗无症状动脉粥样硬化对于减轻全球心血管疾病负担至关重要。我们的结果支持前瞻性研究，评估以成像为指导的预防策略（包括使用便携式超声）是否可以提高当前标准。如果得到证实，这将为最常见的心血管疾病带来精准医疗。”

paras.en: If funded, the second phase of REACT, planned for 2027 to 2032, will examine that question directly.
paras.zh: 如果获得资助，计划于 2027 年至 2032 年进行的 REACT 第二阶段将直接研究这个问题。

paras.en: Researchers intend to launch a large randomized clinical trial testing whether prevention guided by imaging can slow or reduce the systemic progression of atherosclerosis. The longer term goal is to determine whether this strategy can prevent heart attacks, strokes and other cardiovascular events more effectively than current practice.
paras.zh: 研究人员打算开展一项大型随机临床试验，测试影像指导的预防是否可以减缓或减少动脉粥样硬化的全身进展。长期目标是确定该策略是否能够比目前的做法更有效地预防心脏病、中风和其他心血管事件。

paras.en: The research team is also extending REACT beyond Europe to determine whether the findings hold across different populations.
paras.zh: 研究团队还将 REACT 扩展到欧洲以外的地区，以确定这些研究结果是否适用于不同人群。

paras.en: "REACT is expanding its impact around the world. We have established close collaborations with India, Singapore, Tanzania and Mexico to validate these results in populations across the globe," Dr. Ibáñez said.
paras.zh: “REACT 正在扩大其在世界各地的影响。我们已与印度、新加坡、坦桑尼亚和墨西哥建立了密切合作，以在全球人群中验证这些结果，”伊巴涅斯博士说。

paras.en: REACT builds on the earlier PESA-CNIC-Santander study led by Dr. Valentin Fuster, Director General of CNIC, who is also directly involved in REACT.
paras.zh: REACT 建立在早期 PESA-CNIC-Santander 研究的基础上，该研究由 CNIC 总干事 Valentin Fuster 博士领导，他也直接参与了 REACT。

paras.en: That work found that atherosclerosis was already present in many middle aged adults and was associated with lifestyle patterns. REACT extends the investigation into much younger age groups in an effort to understand when the disease first begins to emerge.
paras.zh: 这项研究发现，许多中年成年人已经存在动脉粥样硬化，并且与生活方式有关。 REACT 将调查范围扩大到更年轻的年龄组，以了解这种疾病何时开始出现。

paras.en: "PESA has shown us that atherosclerotic disease is present in many middle-aged people and is associated with lifestyle patterns. In REACT, we wanted to investigate how it emerges at much younger ages. For years, we have proposed that early intervention in atherosclerosis could not only prevent its progression but might even make it possible to cure the disease. REACT will answer this question," Dr. Fuster said.
paras.zh: “PESA 向我们表明，动脉粥样硬化疾病存在于许多中年人身上，并且与生活方式有关。在 REACT 中，我们希望研究这种疾病在更年轻的时候是如何出现的。多年来，我们提出对动脉粥样硬化的早期干预不仅可以阻止其进展，甚至可能使治愈该疾病成为可能。REACT 将回答这个问题，”Fuster 博士说。

paras.en: Materials provided by Centro Nacional de Investigaciones Cardiovasculares Carlos III (F.S.P.). Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
paras.zh: 材料由卡洛斯三世国家心血管研究中心 (F.S.P.) 提供。注意：内容的风格和长度可能会被编辑。
